questions.q: The volume of the eyeball is:
questions.exp: The book lists the volume of the eyeball as 6 ml; 24 ml is a trap — 24 mm is the axial length, not the volume. (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The eyeball is aspherical — specifically an ______.
questions.exp: Shape of the eyeball: aspherical (oblate spheroid) — a sphere flattened at the poles, not elongated as in a prolate spheroid. (Book p1)

questions.q: In the anatomy lab a student is asked for the site of the eyeball. Per the book, the eyeball is housed in the ______.
questions.exp: Site of the eyeball: the orbit, a bony cage; the figure 'Orbit containing eyeball' labels its roof, lateral wall, medial wall and floor. (Book p1)

questions.q: The axial length (anteroposterior diameter) of the eyeball is:
questions.exp: Axial length/antroposterior diameter: 24 mm (2.4 cm) — one of the four headline values on the 'Basic Anatomy of Eyeball' block. (Book p1)

questions.q: Match each attribute of the eyeball with its value — 1) Volume 2) Site 3) Axial length … A) 24 mm (2.4 cm) B) Orbit (bony cage) C) 6 ml
questions.exp: The book's four basic facts: shape aspherical (oblate spheroid), volume 6 ml, site orbit (bony cage), axial length/antroposterior diameter 24 mm (2.4 cm). (Book p1)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled in the 'Orbit containing eyeball' figure EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The figure labels four structures of the orbit — roof, lateral wall, medial wall and floor; a posterior wall is not among the labelled structures. (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The cornea forms the anterior ______ of the outermost layer of the eyeball.
questions.exp: Layers → Outermost: anterior 1/6th is the cornea (transparent, convex shaped, refractive power present), the limbus is the corneo-scleral junction, and the posterior 5/6th is the sclera. (Book p1)

questions.q: The posterior 5/6th of the outermost layer is formed by the:
questions.exp: Outermost layer: posterior 5/6th : Sclera — white (opaque) and covered by the conjunctiva (a transparent mucous membrane); the choroid belongs to the middle uveal tract. (Book p1)

questions.q: All of the following are stated about the cornea EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The cornea is transparent, convex shaped and has refractive power; 'white (opaque)' is the description of the sclera, not the cornea. (Book p1)

questions.q: Match each structure of the outermost layer with its description — 1) Cornea 2) Limbus 3) Sclera … A) Corneo-scleral junction B) White (opaque), covered by conjunctiva C) Transparent, convex, refractive power present
questions.exp: Cornea: transparent, convex, refractive power present; limbus: corneo-scleral junction; sclera: white (opaque), covered by conjunctiva (transparent mucous membrane). (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The sclera is covered by the ______, described as a transparent mucous membrane.
questions.exp: The sclera (posterior 5/6th of the outermost layer) is white (opaque) and covered by the conjunctiva — a transparent mucous membrane. (Book p1)

questions.q: During dissection, a trainee points at the limbus and asks for its identity. The correct reply is:
opts: The angle of the anterior chamber
The most avascular part of the uvea
The junction of iris and ciliary body
questions.exp: The limbus is defined in the layers flowchart as the corneo-scleral junction; the angle of the anterior chamber and the pars plana (most avascular in uvea) are separate structures. (Book p1)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the layers of the eyeball is TRUE?
opts: The uveal tract is the innermost layer
The retina is present both anteriorly and posteriorly
The outermost layer consists of the cornea, limbus and sclera
questions.exp: Outermost = cornea (anterior 1/6th) + limbus (corneo-scleral junction) + sclera (posterior 5/6th). The uveal tract is the middle (vascular) layer, the retina (neurosensory layer) is present only posteriorly, and the sclera is white and opaque. (Book p1)

questions.q: Which part of the eyeball is described as 'white (opaque)' and covered by a transparent mucous membrane?
questions.exp: Posterior 5/6th : Sclera — white (opaque), covered by conjunctiva (transparent mucous membrane); the iris belongs to the middle uveal tract. (Book p1)

questions.q: The middle layer of the eyeball is the:
questions.exp: Layers → Middle: uveal tract (vascular layer) with parts (anterior and posterior): a. iris, b. ciliary body, c. choroid; the retina is the innermost, neurosensory layer. (Book p1)

questions.q: All of the following are parts of the uveal tract EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Uveal tract parts (anterior and posterior): a. iris, b. ciliary body, c. choroid; the sclera is part of the outermost layer. (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The uveal tract is also referred to as the ______ layer.
questions.exp: The book explicitly labels the middle uveal tract as the 'Vascular Layer'; the neurosensory layer is the innermost retina. (Book p1)

questions.q: The innermost layer of the eyeball is the retina, described in the book as the:
questions.exp: Innermost: Retina — a neurosensory layer, present only posteriorly; the vascular layer is the middle uveal tract. (Book p1)

questions.q: Which statement about the retina is TRUE?
opts: It forms the anterior 1/6th of the outer coat
questions.exp: The retina is the innermost neurosensory layer and is present only posteriorly; the middle layer is the vascular uveal tract, the anterior 1/6th is the cornea, and the limbus is the corneo-scleral junction. (Book p1)

questions.q: A medical student must recite the three parts of the uveal tract in the book's order (a, b, c). The correct sequence is:
questions.exp: Uveal tract — Parts (anterior and posterior): a. iris, b. ciliary body, c. choroid, in that order. (Book p1)

questions.q: The anterior chamber (AC) is the space:
opts: Between the cornea and the iris
Between the iris and the lens
questions.exp: The structural anatomy diagram annotates 'Anterior chamber (AC): between cornea and iris'; the posterior chamber (PC) lies deeper, behind the iris. (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The posterior segment of the eyeball contains the ______.
questions.exp: Posterior segment: contains vitreous (1% hyaluronic acid, gel-like consistency); the aqueous humour is in the anterior segment. (Book p1)

questions.q: Match each part of the ciliary body with its feature — 1) Pars plicata 2) Pars plana 3) Ciliary processes … A) Secrete aqueous B) Flat part; most avascular in uvea C) Pleated part
questions.exp: Ciliary body: pars plicata (pleated), pars plana (flat) — most avascular in uvea; the ciliary processes secrete aqueous. (Book p1)

questions.q: Which part of the ciliary body is pleated?
questions.exp: Ciliary body parts: pars plicata (pleated) and pars plana (flat, most avascular in uvea); the ciliary processes secrete aqueous. (Book p1)

questions.q: Fill up: The pars plana is described as ______ in the uvea.
questions.exp: Pars plana (flat) — most avascular in uvea; the pleated part is the pars plicata. (Book p1)

questions.q: During a slit-lamp teaching session a junior asks which structure secretes the aqueous humour. The book's answer is:
questions.exp: In the structural anatomy diagram the ciliary processes are annotated with 'secrete aqueous' — the source of aqueous humour. (Book p1)

questions.q: The vitreous contains ______ hyaluronic acid, with a gel-like consistency.
questions.exp: Posterior segment: contains vitreous → 1% hyaluronic acid, gel-like consistency. (Book p1)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled in the 'Structural anatomy of eyeball' diagram EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The diagram labels the angle of AC, iris, pupil, zonules/ciliary zonules, lens, ciliary body (pars plicata, pars plana), ciliary processes, AC, PC, anterior segment, sclera, choroid and retina; the corneal endothelium is not labelled. (Book p1)

questions.q: Match each segment/chamber of the eyeball with its description — 1) Anterior chamber (AC) 2) Anterior segment (AS) 3) Posterior segment … A) Contains vitreous (1% hyaluronic acid, gel-like) B) Between cornea and iris C) Contains aqueous humour
questions.exp: AC: between cornea and iris; anterior segment (AS): contains aqueous humour; posterior segment: contains vitreous (1% hyaluronic acid, gel-like consistency). (Book p1)

questions.q: In the structural anatomy diagram, the zonules (ciliary zonules) are shown attached to the:
questions.exp: The cross-section labels 'Zonules/ciliary zonules' spanning the ciliary body to the lens, suspending it behind the iris and pupil. (Book p1)

questions.q: Which statement about the eye segments is TRUE?
opts: The anterior segment contains the vitreous
The posterior chamber lies between the cornea and iris
The posterior segment contains the aqueous humour
The anterior segment contains the aqueous humour
questions.exp: Anterior segment (AS): contains aqueous humour; the anterior chamber (not the posterior chamber) lies between cornea and iris; the posterior segment contains the vitreous. (Book p1)

questions.q: In the diagram, the vitreous contained in the posterior segment is annotated with which pair of features?
opts: 25% hyaluronic acid and a fluid consistency
1% hyaluronic acid and a gel-like consistency
No hyaluronic acid and a solid consistency
1% hyaluronic acid and a fluid consistency
questions.exp: Posterior segment: contains vitreous → 1% hyaluronic acid, gel-like consistency — the exact annotation in the structural anatomy diagram. (Book p1)

questions.q: The rate of aqueous humour secretion is:
questions.exp: Aqueous humour — rate of secretion: 2.3 µL/minute; 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg is the outflow value and 6 ml is the eyeball volume. (Book p2)

questions.q: Aqueous outflow is:
questions.exp: Aqueous outflow: 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg — note the unit differs from secretion (2.3 µL/minute); outflow is pressure-dependent, hence per mm Hg. (Book p2)

questions.q: The function of aqueous humour is to exert the intraocular pressure (IOP). IOP is measured by:
questions.exp: Aqueous humour function: exerts intraocular pressure (IOP) — measured by tonometry; tonography is reserved for aqueous outflow. (Book p2)

questions.q: Aqueous outflow is measured by:
questions.exp: Aqueous outflow (0.25 µL/min/mm Hg) is measured by tonography, whereas the IOP it helps generate is measured by tonometry — the classic exam distinction. (Book p2)

questions.q: Aqueous outflow occurs via the ______, whose depth is 3 mm (range 2.5–4.4 mm).
questions.exp: Aqueous outflow: 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg, via the angle of the AC — depth 3 mm (2.5 mm – 4.4 mm). (Book p2)

questions.q: The depth of the anterior chamber, the route of aqueous outflow, is:
questions.exp: Via angle of AC → depth: 3 mm (2.5 mm – 4.4 mm), measured by tonography in the aqueous outflow block. (Book p2)

questions.q: Fill up: Aqueous humour is a fluid secreted from the ______.
questions.exp: Aqueous humour: fluid secreted from the ciliary processes — the same structures annotated 'secrete aqueous' in the structural anatomy diagram. (Book p2)

questions.q: Match each aqueous humour parameter with its value — 1) Rate of secretion 2) Outflow 3) AC depth (route of outflow) … A) 3 mm (2.5–4.4 mm) B) 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg C) 2.3 µL/minute
questions.exp: Rate of secretion 2.3 µL/minute; aqueous outflow 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg via the angle of AC, whose depth is 3 mm (2.5–4.4 mm). (Book p2)

units.title: Basic anatomy of the eyeball — shape, volume, site, axial length and the orbit
units.guide: The chapter opens with four headline values of the eyeball: shape is aspherical (oblate spheroid), volume 6 ml, site the orbit (a bony cage), and axial length/antroposterior diameter 24 mm (2.4 cm). The 'Orbit containing eyeball' figure labels four structures of the orbit — the roof, the lateral wall, the medial wall and the floor — around the globe.

units.title: Outermost coat — cornea, limbus and sclera
units.guide: The outermost layer has three components: the anterior 1/6th is the cornea (transparent, convex shaped, refractive power present), the limbus is the corneo-scleral junction, and the posterior 5/6th is the sclera (white, opaque, covered by the conjunctiva — a transparent mucous membrane). The anterior eye photograph labels the sclera, limbus and the iris with the pupil, both 'seen below cornea'.

units.title: Uveal tract and retina — middle and innermost coats
units.guide: The middle layer is the uveal tract — explicitly labelled the vascular layer — with parts (anterior and posterior): a. iris, b. ciliary body, c. choroid. The innermost layer is the retina, a neurosensory layer that is present only posteriorly, not over the whole globe.

units.title: Structural anatomy — chambers, ciliary body and eye segments
units.guide: The 'Structural anatomy of eyeball' cross-section labels the angle of AC, iris, pupil, zonules (ciliary zonules) and lens. The ciliary body has a pleated pars plicata, a flat pars plana (most avascular in uvea) and ciliary processes that secrete aqueous. The anterior chamber (AC) lies between cornea and iris, the anterior segment (AS) contains aqueous humour, and the posterior segment contains the vitreous — 1% hyaluronic acid with a gel-like consistency.

units.title: Aqueous humour — secretion, outflow and IOP
units.guide: Aqueous humour is a fluid secreted from the ciliary processes at 2.3 µL/minute. Its function is to exert the intraocular pressure (IOP), measured by tonometry. Aqueous outflow is 0.25 µL/min/mm Hg, occurs via the angle of the AC (depth 3 mm, range 2.5–4.4 mm) and is measured by tonography — the tonometry-versus-tonography distinction is the key exam trap on this page.
